title: Oct 14 Results + Oct 15 Preview: Sometimes You Just Tip Your Cap
summary: Oct 14 brought a tough miss, but Oct 15's Rays-Guardians matchup tells a different story

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About October Baseball

Look, I'm not going to sugarcoat it—yesterday was rough. We went 0-for-1 on October 14th, and when you're dealing with a single-game slate in the postseason, there's nowhere to hide. The Dodgers were supposed to have the edge at home against Milwaukee, and instead, the Brewers reminded everyone why October baseball is beautifully, maddeningly unpredictable.

But here's what I love about this process: every miss teaches us something. Every swing and miss in the prediction game makes the next call sharper.

## What Happened in LA

We liked the Dodgers at 56% confidence—not a screaming pick, but a solid lean based on home field and the overall metrics. Milwaukee had other plans. That's postseason baseball for you. The margin for error shrinks, the pressure amplifies, and sometimes the underdog just outplays the favorite.

No excuses, just facts. We move forward.

## Tomorrow's Story: Rays at Guardians

Now let's talk about October 15th, because this is where it gets interesting. We've got Tampa Bay traveling to Cleveland, and our model is leaning toward the Rays at 54%. It's essentially a coin flip with a slight edge—the kind of game that comes down to execution and which pitcher can handle the moment better.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - October 15
content.sub: 54% win probability • Griffin Jax vs Gavin Williams

content.value:
## The Pitching Matchup That Matters

Griffin Jax takes the ball for Tampa Bay, while Gavin Williams gets the nod for Cleveland. Here's the thing about this matchup—it's not about overwhelming stuff or veteran savvy. It's about who can limit the damage and keep their team in striking distance.

The Rays have built their entire identity on doing more with less, on finding edges in the margins. That 54% confidence reflects a tight game where small decisions—a stolen base, a defensive shift, a manager's gut call—could swing the outcome.

Cleveland at home is always tough, but Tampa Bay's got that scrappy energy that plays well in October. We're riding with the Rays, but expect a nail-biter.

## The Bottom Line

Yesterday didn't go our way. Tomorrow's a new opportunity. That's the beautiful thing about baseball—there's always another game, another chance to get it right. The Rays-Guardians matchup might not have the star power of other postseason games, but it's got everything that makes October special: evenly matched teams, quality pitching, and everything on the line.

Let's see if Tampa Bay can deliver.

*— Hana*
